headline: Break a capacity plan before production does
overview: The control room ties growth, storage, traffic, fleet survival, headroom, and cost together. Scenario buttons make the trade-off visible immediately, so this walk records the changed outputs rather than just the sliders.
targetAudience: An engineer sizing a service before a launch

steps.title: The baseline has numbers, not adjectives
steps.action: Opened the capacity-planning control room and moved to the operational scenarios.
steps.description: The baseline quantifies users, replicated storage, scenario RPS, surviving instances, headroom, and monthly cost in one model.
steps.screenshotAlt: Capacity planning baseline and scenario controls

steps.title: A launch more than doubles demand
steps.description: The same fleet is challenged with **2.2× demand**; the scenario output rises from 87.5K to 192.5K RPS, making the capacity risk concrete.
steps.screenshotAlt: Capacity plan under the launch spike scenario

steps.title: The plan survives with one zone gone
steps.description: The model removes a third of the fleet while keeping peak traffic, so the learner can read the new surviving-instance and headroom consequences before touching production.
steps.screenshotAlt: Capacity plan after losing one availability zone

note: Live production evidence. Discovery used Codex computer control; recording used the cross-runtime capture contract so Claude can rerun the same script.
